analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch (head lines ~2336-2348, beyond the two supplied excerpts at lines 1-801) adds a paragraph on Flint constrained-decode chaining and the automatic paged list for RecursiveSI/flint-int4. The supplied units are the head text of lines 1-801, which describe the Nemotron Super slot, GLM5Next and prefix-cache design. This text does not appear in the changed ranges, so I treated it as unchanged context.

Security relevance:
- Prefix-cache text states that Nemotron prefix reuse is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope (T-041). Without a scope it stays cold and never publishes. The Super slot emits no cache receipts. This is consistent with the T-041 scoping posture, and no weakening is visible.
- The Flint patch describes redraw from retained logits with penalty state and per-row RNG restored. That is a performance and correctness note and adds no new trust boundary.
- `maskCacheKey` is the constraint state, so the device mask cache is keyed on state only. The mask depends only on the state, so no cross-tenant data enters the key. This is plausible, but the implementation is not supplied.
- The change to a legacy serving width on M5 Pro, Max and Ultra is a capacity/availability matter (A-001, T-010) and cannot be verified from docs.

No code, controls, keys or protocol changed, so no regression is identified. Remaining questions for integration: whether the chained constrained-decode path (sampling step N+1 before N is confirmed) correctly honours cancellation and per-request isolation, and whether the cached device mask is shared across requests. Both are implementation details outside the supplied evidence and are not findings.
